prompt_text: I need a checkup and cleaning in Pleasanton. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Pleasanton CA for a checkup and cleaning?
answer_verbatim:
For a routine exam and cleaning in Pleasanton, I’d call these offices first—then choose based on who confirms your insurance, new-patient availability, and a transparent estimate:

1. **Pleasanton Valley Dental**  
   **Why call:** A general-dentistry office is usually the best fit for a straightforward checkup, X-rays if needed, and hygiene cleaning. Ask whether they can schedule the exam and cleaning in the same visit; some offices separate them for new patients.

2. **Amador Dental & Orthodontics**  
   **Why call:** A larger, multi-provider practice can be a good option if you need an appointment relatively soon or want the ability to handle follow-up work—such as a filling, crown evaluation, or orthodontic question—without changing offices.

3. **Pleasanton Smile Dental**  
   **Why call:** Worth contacting if you prefer a neighborhood general dentist and want a practice that can establish ongoing preventive care rather than treating this as a one-time cleaning.

4. **Foothill Dental Care**  
   **Why call:** Another sensible general-dentistry option to compare for scheduling, insurance participation, and new-patient policies. It is especially useful to have a second or third office to call because hygiene appointments can book farther out than dentist exams.

5. **Dental Care of Pleasanton**  
   **Why call:** Put this on your call list if convenience, routine preventive care, and a full-service office are priorities. Confirm whether the cleaning will be performed by a hygienist on the first visit and what new-patient X-rays cost if insurance does not cover them.

When you call, use this script:

> “I’m a new patient in Pleasanton and need a routine exam and cleaning. Do you accept **[your insurance plan]**? What is the first available appointment? Can the exam and cleaning be done at the same visit? What would my out-of-pocket estimate be, including X-rays if needed?”

A few things to watch for:
- **“New-patient special” pricing** may not include a standard cleaning if you have gum disease; ask what happens if they recommend periodontal/deep cleaning.  
- Confirm the office is **in-network**, not merely willing to bill your insurance.  
- If you have not been to a dentist in several years, ask whether they reserve enough time for the exam and cleaning in one appointment.  
- If you want the fastest appointment, call when the office opens and ask about cancellations.

If you tell me your insurance carrier, whether you prefer a woman dentist, and roughly which part of Pleasanton you’re in, I can narrow this to the best two or three offices to try first.
